A trip to the big city, that's all.|Parja Bralor|}} '''Keldabe''' was the [[Capital/Legends|capital]] [[City/Legends|city]] of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]], the cultural [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] people, located in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy's]] [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]. Situated atop a flat [[Granite/Legends|granite]] hill forty-five degrees north of the planetary equator, the urban [[Fortress/Legends|fort]]-town of Keldabe was almost completely surrounded by a bend in the [[Kelita River]] and the [[Tree/Legends|forests]] of Mandalore's north. Packed with an eclectic array of buildings of all shapes and material, ranging from [[Durasteel/Legends|durasteel]] to [[Veshok|wood]], Keldabe was a hub for life on Mandalore, and boasted landmarks such as the hundred-[[Meter/Legends|meter]]-tall [[MandalMotors tower|tower]] of the [[MandalMotors/Legends|MandalMotors]] company, along with the ''[[Oyu'baat]]'', the oldest [[Cantina/Legends|cantina]] on the planet. The ''Oyu'baat'' was a common gathering place for Keldabe residents and Mandalorian clan [[Chief/Legends|leaders]], and twice a [[Standard week/Legends|week]] Keldabe's streets were packed as Mandalorians bought and sold goods on market [[Standard day/Legends|days]]. Founded at a [[Time/Legends|time]] prior to the [[Mandalorian Wars]], Keldabe not only became Mandalore's planetary capital, but the governmental center for the surrounding [[Mandalore sector/Legends|Mandalore sector]]. Following the [[Mandalorian Excision|rise]] of the [[New Mandalorians/Legends|New Mandalorians]], Keldabe stood alongside the pacifist faction's [[Domed city/Legends|domed]] capital, [[Sundari/Legends|Sundari]], and during the later part of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], MandalMotors' Keldabe facilities were seized by [[Spar|Mandalore the Resurrector]] for use by the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]]. As the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] was [[Declaration of a New Order|transformed]] into the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], an Imperial [[Garrison/Legends|garrison]] was established just south of Keldabe at the [[City of Bone]], leading to a noticeable presence of Imperial [[Stormtrooper/Legends|troops]] wandering the Keldabe streets while on leave. Around this same time, Keldabe was chosen by the members of [[Clan Skirata]] to be the point where they spread a [[nanovirus]] immunogen, knowing that Keldabe's role as a planetary hub would ensure the curative vaccine spread across Mandalore and protect it from Imperial [[FG36|viral weaponry]]. During the [[Yuuzhan Vong War|war]] with the [[Yuuzhan Vong]], Keldabe and the surrounding area sustained damage when the [[Yuuzhan Vong galaxy|extra-galactic]] [[Alien/Legends|aliens]] [[Battle of Mandalore (Yuuzhan Vong War)|attacked]] Mandalore, leaving buildings scarred and the nearby woodland flattened for [[Standard decade/Legends|decades]] after. ==Description== {{Quote|Someone better tell him the ''Oyu'baat'' is as five-star as we get in Keldabe.|Boba Fett, referring to the [[Coruscanti/Legends|Coruscanti]] [[Doctor/Legends|doctor]], [[Beluine]]|}} The [[Capital/Legends|capital]] [[City/Legends|city]] of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] [[Planet/Legends|world]] of [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]], Keldabe was located forty-five degrees north of the planetary equator, and was situated at the top of a flat hill made of [[Granite/Legends|granite]] at a bend in the [[Kelita River]]. The [[river]] bend nearly encircled the city in its entirety, forming something of a natural moat around Keldabe that only widened as [[Time/Legends|time]] went on; a number of bridges were constructed to pass over the Kelita, allowing travelers to enter the city on [[Limb/Legends|foot]]. Taking its name from the [[Mando'a/Legends|''Mando'a'']] word ''keldab''—meaning "citadel" or "stronghold"{{WebCite|url=http://www.karentraviss.com/page20/page26/index.html|text=Mando'a|author=Karen Traviss|work=[http://www.karentraviss.com Karen Traviss]|archivedate=20110925083955}}—Keldabe sat atop the granite outcrop as an example of a large [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] hill-[[Fortress/Legends|fort]] town. A durable stone balustrade was erected as a barrier between the city's raised outer edge and the sheer drop from the hill top into the fast-moving Kelita River below. At one point, a [[Mining sluice|sluice gate]] was constructed in the lower parts of Keldabe nearest to the river level, but it was eventually removed and the stone archway at the end of the alley that had led to it was railed off. Spray from the Kelita soaked the Keldabe alley with [[Water/Legends|water]], leading to dark [[Color/Legends|green]] [[frond-grass]] growing abundantly among the cracks in the stone arch, and its out of the way location made the alley a perfect place for private contemplation, a secret meeting with a lover, or simply hiding out. The air around Keldabe smelled of the sweet woody scent of resin [[Tree/Legends|trees]]. Keldabe was a densely packed city, with its numerous buildings erected in close quarters to each other. The architecture was varied in its design from one building to another, as were the materials used in their construction, ranging from stone and wood, to [[Plastoid/Legends|plastoid]] and [[Durasteel/Legends|durasteel]]. The city's layout defied conventional standards of town planning, and was considered by some to be cramped and disorganized, with streets that were narrow compared to those of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], and alleys that were often overhung by surrounding buildings. Portions of the city were left unchanged for [[Standard century/Legends|centuries]], allowing old wood-framed buildings of [[plaster]] to be found side by side with industrial warehouses and polished granite towers. Keldabe boasted an assortment of [[Tapcafe/Legends|tapcafs]] offering refreshments such as mugs of [[shig]], a hot Mandalorian [[Tea/Legends|beverage]],{{InsiderCite|86|The Mandalorians: People and Culture}} and a variety of shops, selling an array of goods including tools, machine parts, [[Blaster/Legends|blasters]] and bladed weaponry, [[holozine]]s, toiletries, and [[Wine/Legends|wine]]. A number of tapcafs and shops could be found lining the length of [[Chortav Meshurkaane]]—"Gem-Cutter's Street" in Basic. Twice a [[Standard week/Legends|week]], on Keldabe's market [[Standard day/Legends|days]], Chortav Meshurkaane was filled with market stalls selling items ranging from precious metals and [[Gemstone/Legends|gemstones]] to [[Leather/Legends|leather]] goods, including [[Glove/Legends|gloves]], [[Utility belt/Legends|belts]], and [[Kama/Legends|''kamas'']]. One end of Chortav Meshurkaane opened onto an ancient paved square that during market days was often filled with stalls selling [[Foodstuff/Legends|food]], attracting a heavy presence of drinkers and shoppers who flocked to the numerous merchant stalls that sprung up around the city. Across the ancient square from Chortav Meshurkaane was the ''[[Oyu'baat]]'' tapcaf, the oldest [[Cantina/Legends|cantina]] on the planet Mandalore. The ''Oyu'baat''{{'s}} prominence made it a convenient and popular meeting place for Mandalorians in the Keldabe area, and the tapcaf served as an unofficial center for the loose government formed by the Mandalorian warrior clans for much of Mandalore's history. That duty was shared with the communal building known as [[MandalMotors Hall]], after it was constructed in Keldabe and donated to the clans by the [[MandalMotors/Legends|MandalMotors]] company in [[40 ABY/Legends|40 ABY]]. By that same [[Standard year/Legends|year]], Keldabe was home to [[Hayca Mekket's veterinary office]]s, [[Cikartan's tapcaf]], and [[Novoc Vevut's home]], where the Mandalorian [[Soldier/Legends|soldier]] lived with [[Clan Vevut|his clan]] and crafted weapons in the attached workshop. One of Keldabe's most renowned landmarks was MandalMotors' [[MandalMotors tower|tower]] headquarters, which stood one hundred [[Meter/Legends|meters]] tall and was adorned with the company's [[Mythosaur/Legends|mythosaur]] [[Bone/Legends|skull]] logo. The tower became a common point of reference for [[Pilot/Legends|pilots]] navigating around the [[Keldabe spaceport]], and could be seen from as far away as the small suburb of [[Bralsin]]. An open air animal market sat at the outer edge of Keldabe, and on the outskirts of the city, Mandalorian domains could be found built into the trunks and branches of trees amidst the [[Veshok|woodland]] surroundings. It was near the city that the [[Mandalorian forest encampment|forest encampment]] used by the [[Mandalorian Protectors (Spar)|Mandalorian Protectors]] during the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire's]] occupation of Mandalore was located.[[Star Wars (1977) 68|''Star Wars'' (1977) 68]] Nearly ten [[Kilometer/Legends|kilometers]] outside of Keldabe sat the [[Beviin-Vasur farm]], as well as [[Levet's farm|the farm]] belonging to the Mandalorian named [[Levet]]. ==History== ===Early history through the Clone Wars=== {{Quote|Nice day out, ''Kad'ika!'' See all the funny ''Mando'ade'' playing with knives and blasters, and singing rude songs?''"
"''I think ''you'' get more excited about a day out in Keldabe than he does. It's good to see you happy again, son.|Fi and [[Kal Skirata]], talking to and about the infant [[Venku Skirata]]|}} Founded at a time prior to the onset of the [[Mandalorian Wars]], Keldabe established itself as the capital city of the Mandalorians' cultural [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of Mandalore. Though the planet was largely abandoned by the [[Mandalorian Crusaders]] under [[Mandalore the Indomitable]] during the [[Great Sith War/Legends|Great Sith War]] in [[3996 BBY]], as [[Mandalore the Ultimate]] led the [[Mandalorian Neo-Crusaders/Legends|Mandalorian Neo-Crusaders]] to expand the [[Mandalore sector/Legends|Mandalore sector]] through conquest, Keldabe became the governmental center for all of Mandalorian [[Realspace/Legends|space]]. In the aftermath of the [[Mandalorian Excision]] of [[738 BBY]]—a brief but overwhelming [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]]-led assault on the Mandalore sector by the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], orchestrated to curb a rise in Mandalorian militancy so soon after the [[Seventh Battle of Ruusan|end]] of the [[New Sith Wars]] that frightened the Republic—the pacifist [[New Mandalorians/Legends|New Mandalorian]] faction arose, espousing peace''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'' and establishing their own capital in the [[Desert/Legends|desert]] wastes''[[The Clone Wars: Darth Maul: Shadow Conspiracy]]'' left behind by the Excision, the [[Domed city/Legends|domed city]] of [[Sundari/Legends|Sundari]], that existed alongside Keldabe. At one point, a sluice gate was constructed at the edge of Keldabe and into the Kelita River, though it was later removed and the pathway leading to it was barred. Several hundred years before the [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|start]] of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the Mandalorian [[Mandalorian shock trooper|shocktrooper]] [[Gustav Zenlav]] founded the MandalMotors company, headquartering the enterprise in Keldabe.{{InsiderCite|80|The History of the Mandalorians: Exploring the Evolution of a Mighty Race of Warriors}} The one hundred-meter-tall tower of MandalMotors became a Keldabe landmark, with many a Mandalorian pilot making use of the tower to navigate their way to Keldabe's [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceport]] by [[Eye/Legends|eye]]. Late in the [[Cloning/Legends|Clone]] Wars, MandalMotors' headquarters was seized by the Mandalorian Protectors under the command of [[Spar|Mandalore the Resurrector]]. Having allied his world and people with the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] during the war against the Galactic Republic,''[[Galaxy at War]]'' Mandalore the Resurrector ensured that MandalMotors' Keldabe facilities were put to exclusive use for the Confederacy. After the Mandalorian Protectors were defeated and largely [[Mission to Norval II|destroyed]] at [[Norval II]], the [[Army/Legends|army's]] three survivors—[[Fenn Shysa]], [[Tobbi Dala]], and Spar, the former Mandalore the Resurrector who resigned from his post after the devastating loss—returned to Mandalore. There, Shysa and Spar met with the former [[Clone commando/Legends|clone commando]] [[Fi Skirata]] and his girlfriend [[Parja Bralor]], at the ''Oyu'baat'' tapcaf in Keldabe, where they attempted to get the clone of one-time ''Mand'alor'' [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]] to step up as Fett's lost heir and claim the title of ''Mand'alor'', himself. Skirata declined, however, and Shysa later acquiesced to popular opinion and took up the position himself at the end of the Clone Wars. ===Imperial occupation=== {{Quote|Do you see the Keldabe garrison as an occupying army?''"
"''You would, if this was Gibad.''"
"''But your leader let them come here and rent land.''"
"''We're in no shape to fight that big an army. If Shysa had told them to get lost, you know what would have happened next. Better to watch and wait. Build our strength.|[[Ovolot Qail Uthan]] and Kal Skirata|}} Though the people of Keldabe celebrated, most were unaware that Shysa had only become the new ''Mand'alor'' in response to the newly [[Declaration of a New Order|risen]] Galactic Empire's interest in a [[Garrison/Legends|garrison]] on Mandalore, and Shysa's own misgivings toward an Imperial presence that had been ratified by the clans in need of the [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|funds]] the Empire had offered. South of the Kelita River bend that surrounded Keldabe, an [[Hayar's brother|enterprising Mandalorian]] had constructed a theme park in the shape of a [[Mythosaur/Legends|mythosaur]] [[Skeleton/Legends|skeleton]] in the hopes of attracting offworld tourism. The park, known as the [[City of Bone]],[[Star Wars (1977) 69|''Star Wars'' (1977) 69]] never opened, but when the Empire arrived on Mandalore, a group of Mandalorians including the park's founder, his brother [[Hayar]], and friend [[Jarkyc]], convinced the [[Unidentified Imperial commander (Mandalore)|Imperial commander]] that the structure was in fact a Mandalorian temple of great [[Mandalorian religion|religious]] significance to the people, prompting the Empire to purchase the defunct park and establish the Imperial base and garrison inside it. The new base's proximity to Keldabe made the city a prime target for Imperial [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] to walk about during their afforded leave from the base, though [[Unidentified Oyu'baat bartender|the bartender]] of the ''[[Oyu'baat]]'' cantina ensured the Empire's [[Troop/Legends|troops]] stayed out of his establishment. It was around this time that [[Clan Skirata]] ventured into Keldabe in order to covertly spread an immunogen designed to inoculate an individual against the Empire's [[Death/Legends|deadly]] [[FG36]] [[nanovirus]]. Walking the streets of Keldabe on one of the city's market days, the infectious members of the Skirata clan propagated the cure to dozens of unwitting others as they would the [[Cold/Legends|common cold]], by breath or by touch, knowing that Keldabe's nature as a social hub for the entire planet would lead to the immunogen's dispersal across all of Mandalore. During the trip, however, [[Mij Gilamar]]—a close friend of Clan Skirata—had a run in with the [[Death Watch/Legends|Death Watch]] member, [[Dred Priest]], that turned violent. Priest was [[Knife/Legends|stabbed]] and killed by Gilamar, and his body dumped into the Kelita River. Around [[18 BBY/Legends|18 BBY]], the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]]-in-hiding [[Jax Pavan]] journeyed to Mandalore in pursuit of information on the whereabouts of his friend, [[Thi Xon Yimmon]], leader of the anti-Imperial [[Whiplash]] organization. Touching down at the Keldabe spaceport, Pavan donned a [[Scoundrel/Legends|scoundrel's]] disguise and set out for the ''Oyu'baat'' cantina seeking the aid and resources of [[Black Sun/Legends|Black Sun]] [[Lieutenant/Legends|lieutenant]] [[Tyno Fabris]], who had set up an office in the ancient tapcaf in order to oversee the crime syndicate's dealings on Mandalore and its [[Moon/Legends|moon]], [[Concordia/Legends|Concordia]]. While Pavan made contact with Fabris at the ''Oyu'baat'' and attempted to negotiate a bargain, the Jedi's traveling companions [[Den Dhur]] and the [[Droid/Legends|droid]] [[I-5YQ]] went to a [[Keldabe warehouse store]] to shop for parts in order to upgrade the [[5YQ-series protocol droid]]. Pavan's meetings with Fabris drew the attention of Fabris' superior, the [[Falleen/Legends|Falleen]] Black Sun [[Vigo/Legends|vigo]] known as [[Xizor/Legends|Xizor]], who knew Pavan from a [[Battle in the Factory District|previous encounter]] and traveled to Keldabe in order to broker a deal in person, a deal in which Xizor would provide his aid in Pavan's search for Yimmon in return for a valuable favor of his choosing from the Jedi Knight. Though Pavan relented to Xizor's terms, the vigo later went back on their bargain, leading to a [[Skirmish in the Oyu'baat|shootout]] at the ''Oyu'baat'' from which Pavan was forced to flee, departing Keldabe with his comrades aboard [[Laranth|their ship]] shortly after, leaving Mandalore for [[Kantaros Station]] in [[Bothan Space/Legends|Bothan space]].[[The Last Jedi (novel)|''The Last Jedi'']] The Empire's presence on Mandalore eventually turned from cordial to hostile, occupying the Mandalorian homeworld, enslaving the Mandalorian people, and strip-[[Mining/Legends|mining]] the planet for valuable [[Beskar/Legends|''beskar'']] [[Iron/Legends|iron]] [[Ore/Legends|ore]]. In opposition to the Empire, ''Mand'alor'' Fenn Shysa established a second generation of the Mandalorian Protectors as an insurgent force that waged a guerrilla war against the Imperials from their encampment in the forests within walking distance of Keldabe. During the occupation, Imperial advisors were placed on MandalMotors' executive board at the behest of the Empire. These advisors allowed the company to remain in business under the Empire's reign, and during that time, MandalMotors developed the [[Keldabe-class cruiser|''Keldabe''-class battleship]], producing it''[[Rebellion Era Campaign Guide]]'' alongside [[Mandal Hypernautics Corporation|Mandal Hypernautics]]. The powerful [[Warship/Legends|battleship]] was named for the Mandalorian capital.''[[Star Wars: Empire at War: Forces of Corruption]]'' After [[Battle of the City of Bone|destroying]] the City of Bone and ousting the Empire from Mandalorian space, the Mandalorian Protectors reclaimed Keldabe and established a lockdown on the [[Sector/Legends|sector]], patrolled by a [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]] of [[Pursuer-class enforcement ship|''Pursuer''-class enforcement ships]]. When a hostile [[Capital ship/Legends|capital ship]] entered Mandalorian space unauthorized, the Protectors would board the vessel, capture its [[Bridge (starship)/Legends|bridge]], and deliver the ship to the spaceport in Keldabe. ===Yuuzhan Vong War and Mandalore's resurgence=== {{Quote|What do you want, make Keldabe a tourist spot or something? I can see it now. Visit Mandalore before Mandalore visits you. Take home some souvenirs—a slab of ''uj'' cake and a smack in the mouth.|[[Baltan Carid]]|}} In [[25 ABY/Legends|25 ABY]], the undercover [[Yuuzhan Vong]] [[Scout/Legends|scout]], [[Nom Anor]], traveled to Keldabe to meet with [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]]—who had replaced Fenn Shysa as ''Mand'alor'' upon his death—under the guise of the assumed name "Udelen." There, Anor and Fett discussed future prospects for Mandalorian employment during the [[Yuuzhan Vong War|war]] Anor warned was coming, all while under the watchful eye of a [[Keldabe Air Traffic Control]]ler. When the truth of Anor's identity and the [[Yuuzhan Vong empire|Yuuzhan Vong's]] plans for [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] came to light, Fett pledged the Mandalorians' support for the [[Yuuzhan Vong galaxy|extra-galactic]] [[Alien/Legends|aliens]] in exchange for amnesty for the Mandalore sector, all the while secretly intending to gather intelligence and [[Saboteur/Legends|sabotage]] the Yuuzhan Vong's efforts from the inside. When the Yuuzhan Vong discovered Fett's duplicity, they struck back at the Mandalorians by launching an [[Battle of Mandalore (Yuuzhan Vong War)|assault]] on Mandalore that severely damaged portions of Keldabe and flattened large swaths of the nearby forest. Even [[Standard decade/Legends|decades]] after the attack, a number of Keldabe buildings still bore the scars, including MandalMotors' tower. By the start of the [[Second Galactic Civil War]], Boba Fett had come to reside at the [[Farm/Legends|farm]] belonging to his friend [[Goran Beviin]], on the outskirts of Keldabe, a city he had once described as resembling a run-down factory complex someone had dropped in a forest. Fett's granddaughter, [[Mirta Gev]], had joined her lover [[Ghes Orade]] and his [[Parent/Legends|father]], [[Novoc Vevut]], at his Keldabe home. The two [[Clan Fett|Fett family]] members became regular patrons of the ''Oyu'baat'' cantina, and in 40 [[Galactic Standard Calendar|ABY]], both Fett and Gev attended a meeting of Mandalorian clan [[Chief/Legends|leaders]], industry [[Chief Executive Officer/Legends|heads]], and other Mandalorian soldiers at MandalMotors Hall in Keldabe, where the topic of discussion was Mandalore's place in the emerging galactic conflict. There, Fett decreed Mandalore neutral in the war, and as ''Mand'alor'', summoned two million Mandalorians living in diaspora throughout the galaxy to journey to Mandalore in order to rebuild the damage done to the planet by the Yuuzhan Vong. As far-away Mandalorians arrived on Mandalore, the population of the world and Keldabe swelled; the discovery of a new lode of ''beskar'' iron near the town of [[Enceri]] led to a prosperous industrial period for MandalMotors, whose Keldabe facilities churned out powerful new ships with the ''beskar'', including the ''[[Bes'uliik]]''-class [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] and the [[Tra'kad-class transport|''Tra'kad''-class]] [[Assault ship/Legends|assault ship]]. During the galactic [[Galactic Cup of Limmie|bolo-ball tournament]] of [[41 ABY]], Keldabe residents packed the ''Oyu'baat'' to watch the [[Limmie/Legends|games]] on the cantina's large [[Viewscreen/Legends|viewscreen]]. That same year, Mirta Gev and Ghes Orade were [[Wedding of Ghes Orade and Mirta Gev|married]], and a large, festive reception was held at Orade's Keldabe home. ==Behind the scenes== {{Quote|I'll set down near that large forest and we can make our way to the capital city, ''Kedalbe'', on foot.|[[Princess/Legends|Princess]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] introduces the Mandalorian capital to ''Star Wars'' canon in ''Star Wars 68: The Search Begins''|}} In [[February]] of [[1983]], the capital city of Mandalore was first introduced to ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]] in [[Marvel Comics]]'s [[Star Wars (1977)|''Star Wars'']] [[Star Wars comic books|series]]. Called "Kedalbe" in the comic series' [[Star Wars (1977) 68|sixty-eighth issue]], the city would later appear as the similar but differently spelled "Keldabe" in [[Abel G. Peña]]'s [[2005]] article for [[Star Wars Insider]], [[The History of the Mandalorians: Exploring the Evolution of a Mighty Race of Warriors|''The History of the Mandalorians'']]. While creating the fictional ''Mando'a'' language, [[Author/Legends|author]] [[Karen Traviss]] established that the word Keldabe was the plural form of the Mandalorian word ''keldab'', meaning citadel or stronghold. Traviss also used the new Keldabe spelling in the [[EBook|e-novella]] ''[[Boba Fett: A Practical Man]]'', her ''[[Star Wars: Legacy of the Force]]'' entries ''[[Legacy of the Force: Sacrifice]]'' and ''[[Legacy of the Force: Revelation]]'', and her [[Republic Commando|''Republic'' and ''Imperial Commando'' novel series]]. The ''[[Star Wars: Empire at War: Forces of Corruption]]'' [[Star Wars video games|video game]], the ''[[Rebellion Era Campaign Guide]]'', and ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'' also make use of the more recent Keldabe spelling.''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'' Despite this widespread use, ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' by [[Jason Fry]] and [[Daniel Wallace]], reused the original Kedalbe spelling. This article assumes the ''Atlas'' was in error in this respect, and favors the Keldabe spelling as it has been the most widespread in canon. The [[Dorling Kindersley]] reference book [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: What Is a Sith Warrior?|''What Is a Sith Warrior?'']], written by [[Glenn Dakin]], mistakes the New Mandalorian capital of Sundari for Keldabe when referring to the events of the [[Attack on the Memorial Shrine/Legends|bombing of the Memorial Shrine]],''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: What Is a Sith Warrior?]]'' as seen in "[[The Mandalore Plot]]."{{TCW|The Mandalore Plot}} ==Appearances== *''[[Republic Commando: True Colors]]'' {{Mo}} *''[[Order 66: A Republic Commando Novel]]'' *''[[Imperial Commando: 501st]]'' *[[The Last Jedi (novel)|''The Last Jedi'']] *''[[Star Wars: Empire at War: Forces of Corruption]]'' {{Mo}} *[[Star Wars (1977) 68|''Star Wars'' (1977) 68]] {{Reprint|Star Wars (1977) 68}} {{C|First mentioned as "Kedalbe"}} *''[[Boba Fett: A Practical Man]]'' *''[[Legacy of the Force: Sacrifice]]'' *''[[Legacy of the Force: Revelation]]'' *''[[Legacy of the Force: Invincible]]'' {{Mo}} ==Sources== *{{InsiderCite|80|The History of the Mandalorians: Exploring the Evolution of a Mighty Race of Warriors}} {{1stID|"Keldabe"}} *{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/member/insideronline/96/indexp2.html|series=Aliens in the Empire|text=Part 1: Hierarchy of Power}} *''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'' *''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' *''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: What Is a Sith Warrior?]]'' ==Notes and references== {{Reflist}} {{Interlang |de=Keldabe |es=Keldabe |pl=Keldabe }} [[Category:Capital cities]] [[Category:Mandalore locations]]
